title: Coffee Chat on MMM
summary: Three questions to connect the whole marketing investment to the next business decision.
text: Every CMO knows this meeting. The CFO slides the budget across the table and asks one question. Prove it or lose it. My own budget was cut twice in 10 years. Once for COVID, once for a measurement battle we frankly got wrong. What's helped me since is checking whether the measurement covers the same ground as the budget. Creator spend, influencer packages, retail media, the deals that never touch a dashboard. If those are missing from the picture, it's harder to explain what the whole investment is doing. So, I come back to three questions. Can you see every spend line? Can you compare what each one contributed? And does the answer arrive in time to help with the next decision? The thing I wish I'd had then back when I had legacy MMM is what we have today. Full Commerce MMM. The real full picture of go-to-market investments. all 10 spend lines in one picture. And the third question is where most enterprises fall down. The insight arrives, but the action doesn't. Not in time to change the next decision. This is a whole new world, though. Um, an AI interface that's learned on 10 years of MMM expert context, not just Claude or ChatGPT. Ask the question in plain language, run a live simulation in the meeting, and act on it while the market is still there. That's what keeps me engaged. what's possible. Now, I've sat in that chair for 20 plus years as a CMO. These days, I'm focused on paying it forward, sharing what I learned with the next generation of leaders. The shift that helped me most is being able to sit down with finance and say, "Here's what we're seeing. Here's what we've learned, and here's where the next dollar could help us grow. Faster, smarter, better decisions." If that's you, let's chat or start with my AI twin on aicatalyst.biz. It knows how I think about this.
thumbnailAlt: Randy in Coffee Chat on MMM
takeaway: AI Catalyst’s Randy Weyersberg explains how marketing measurement should connect the full investment picture to the next business decision. His three questions are whether every spend line is visible, whether contributions can be compared, and whether the answer arrives in time to act.

faq.answer: Randy Weyersberg proposes three questions: can you see every spend line, compare what each contributed, and get the answer in time for the next decision?

faq.question: Which investments does Randy say can be missed?
faq.answer: The Coffee Chat names creator spend, influencer packages, retail media and deals that never reach a dashboard. Randy argues that missing investments make the overall picture harder to explain.

faq.question: How should measurement support action?
faq.answer: In this Coffee Chat, Randy describes asking questions in plain language and running a simulation during a meeting, so the findings can inform the next investment decision.

title: Coffee Chat on Agentic Live Selling
summary: Randy explores brand agents, individual shopping conversations and scheduled live selling shows.
text: You proved it. The budget's yours. Now comes the harder question. Where does the next dollar go? Search, the front door of the internet for 20 years, is shifting. Your customer doesn't search anymore. Their agent does. 10 million people set up Meta's Muse in 6 weeks in the US and Canada alone. Amazon blocked it. Walmart and Shopify opened the door. And look at Google. Half a trillion dollars gone in a single day. Its worst day ever. Its own AI answers are eating its search ads. That's the market pricing in the end of the search box. So when your customer's agent comes knocking, who meets them? The way I look at it, the next dollar doesn't go to the search box. It goes to a brand agent on your own storefront, a digital human, your best salesperson, one-to-one around the clock, connected to your real inventory, your bundles, your margin. The experience hasn't changed in 25 years. Search box, scroll, click, the death scroll. The agent ends that. Just a conversation. And a conversation qualifies, guides, and converts. So the traffic you get is better traffic. More of what we buy happens online every year. If no one's there to meet that agent, the opportunity is gone. There's a second way in, one to many. a live show at a set time for a special launch, your brand agent hosting it, or even an influencer’s twin as your brand agent. Real people joining in. Folks love being part of an exclusive event. When the conversation happens, one-to-one or one to many, it's built around the customer. That's what drives higher consideration. The brands that build this now are the ones the agents recommend first. That's Agentic Commerce. I've spent 20 plus years as a CMO. These days, I'm focused on paying it forward, sharing what I learned with the next generation of leaders. Faster, smarter, better decisions. If that's you, let's chat or start with my AI twin on aicatalyst.biz. It knows how I think about this.
thumbnailAlt: Randy in Coffee Chat on Agentic Live Selling
takeaway: AI Catalyst’s Randy Weyersberg describes two formats for agentic selling: a storefront brand agent serving an individual shopper or shopper’s agent, and a scheduled live show hosted by a brand agent for real consumers. Both formats should be built around the customer and grounded in the brand’s actual offer.

faq.question: How does one-to-one selling differ from a live show?
faq.answer: One-to-one selling supports an individual customer or customer’s agent. In the scheduled one-to-many format described by Randy, real consumers join a live event hosted by a brand agent.

faq.question: Can an influencer’s digital twin host a selling show?
faq.answer: Randy describes an influencer’s twin acting as the brand agent for a scheduled launch show. The audience in that format is real people, not their shopping agents.

faq.question: What business information should a storefront agent use?
faq.answer: The Coffee Chat names real inventory, bundles and margin. Randy’s proposed storefront agent connects the conversation to that business context rather than offering a generic search box.

title: Coffee Chat on AI Training
summary: Turn AI training into a working agent for one real team workflow, with human judgment built in.
thumbnailAlt: Randy in Coffee Chat on AI Training
text: A CEO said to me, "I paid for the training. My team did the course. Nothing changed." That's the gap. It's not that people don't finish the course. It's that most finish it and Monday morning the work is exactly the same. The learning never becomes the workflow. AI stays a side activity, something people try when they have a spare minute, which they never do. And the CEO is the one who feels it. They're accountable for transforming how the organization works around AI. They encouraged the training, approved the spend for the training, and they're still waiting for the workflows to change. Now, they're impatient. They want action. Here's the number. 88% of people use AI at work now. But only 5% use it in a way that actually changes how they work. The rest are searching and summarizing faster, but the work itself hasn't changed. That's the gap. And in my opinion, online courses don't work when you're trying to learn AI. It's evolving so fast, your module is outdated in 8 weeks. So we built the training the way it was meant to be done. One method, every function. We start with a real problem, one specific piece of work that the team identifies as a target for faster, smarter, and better decisions. We map the workflow step by step where AI helps and where human judgment stays in control. Then we build the agent together in the session and we test it on live work right there until it holds up. It works the same way for every function, marketing, sales, finance, operations, even leadership groups. Same method customized to the work in person or live virtually. And everyone leaves with a completed agent set of instructions for that piece of work. Not notes. Not a demo. Something built, tested, and ready to use on Monday. That's the whole idea. Tools give you the power. Workflows give you the path. And the behavior using it every week is what makes it stick. One method, every function. If you're the one accountable for making AI real in your organization, start with one team and one problem. Ask for details or ask my AI twin at aicatalyst.biz. It knows how I think about this.
takeaway: AI Catalyst’s AI training starts with one team and one real business problem. Randy Weyersberg describes mapping the workflow, deciding where AI helps and where human judgment stays in control, then building and testing an agent together on live work. The intended output is a usable set of agent instructions, supported by regular use after the session.

faq.question: What do participants build during AI training?
faq.answer: Randy describes a completed set of agent instructions for a specific piece of work, built together and tested on live work during the session.

faq.question: Which teams and delivery formats does Randy describe?
faq.answer: The method is adapted to marketing, sales, finance, operations and leadership groups. The Coffee Chat describes in-person sessions or live virtual delivery, customized to the team’s work.

faq.question: Where does human judgment remain in the workflow?
faq.answer: Before building the agent, the team maps the work step by step and identifies where AI can help and where human judgment stays in control. Randy also emphasizes using the workflow every week.
